task: Fix the data encoding corruption after the character encoding was changed from UTF-8 to Latin-1.

candidate_memories.content: International characters in user records are corrupted after the database connection encoding was changed to Latin-1.
The database connection must use UTF-8 encoding; the connection string must specify charset=utf8mb4.
The encoding was changed in the connection pool config during a maintenance window without testing international data.
Only records created or updated after the encoding change are corrupted; older records are intact.
Session 3 note: the localization team reported corrupted international characters in user records during acceptance testing.
MySQL is the production database; the database schema uses utf8mb4 for all text columns.
Session 4 note: the data team added a character set validation check to the migration runbook.
Old practice: Latin-1 was the default encoding before the team adopted internationalization.
The ORM connection pool is configured in database.yaml with the charset parameter.
Session 9 note: the QA team added international character test cases to the user registration suite.
Old encoding guide: the Latin-1 encoding was used during the initial prototype for the single-language MVP.
Database connections must always specify the character encoding explicitly to prevent implicit encoding mismatches.
Session 6 note: the frontend team added emoji support to the user profile display.
The database server is configured with character-set-server=utf8mb4 as the default.
A data quality report in session 11 showed zero encoding errors across all existing records.
Read replicas also use utf8mb4; the encoding is consistent across primary and replicas.
Character encoding must be validated end-to-end from the connection layer to the storage layer.
Session 7 note: the localization team added support for Japanese and Korean user interfaces.
Old connection guide: the pool was configured without a charset parameter and relied on the server default.
The database migration tooling always runs with explicit charset=utf8mb4 in its connection parameters.
